title: Primordial Paradox TALK personas
description: The persona cards for the live talk outside a fight (card t_acae7c0a, spec 21 section 11): Konrad in S1, Urien in S2 and one panicking townsperson in S3, per knowledge/SCENES-S1-S3.md. tools/ai_bridge.py reads this file and nothing else reads it, so the schema is the published shape and the bridge is the enforcer. Two rules a schema cannot state and the bridge checks instead: banned_words, banned_marks and mood_allowed are guards on the answer and are never sent to the model, and a persona answer is capped at two sentences drawn as two lines of 28 characters. Every string here is printable ASCII, because the box draws the sheet's alphabet and a mark the sheet lacks would be a hole.

version.description: Bumped when a voice, a ban or a cap changes, because the bridge hashes the block into its cache key.

rule.description: One line naming who owns the file and what reads it, the way data/talk_cards.json carries its rule line.

sentences.description: Two sentences. The bridge cuts at the second sentence end and labels the repair.

lines.description: At most two box lines, so a persona answer can never fill the message window.

chars.description: The box's own line width (spec 05), unchanged from the fight talk.

budget_s.description: The fight talk's own deadline. A persona request is not given a longer one.

profanity.description: The guard token file the reply is filtered through, data/talk_profanity.json.

personas.description: One card per scene the live talk stands in. Three, because the demo's story beats are three.

line.description: One drawable reply line: printable ASCII, 56 characters at most (two box lines of 28), fitted by the bridge's wrap.

playerLine.description: A bake line, written as the player would type it in the box. 120 characters is the box's cap (spec 21 section 1).

banWord.description: A token the reply may never carry, matched case insensitively on whole words. Held here and never sent to the model.

name.description: The name the box prints, in the sheet's capitals. A persona with no name plate uses its role.

aliases.description: Other names a caller may use for this persona, so a card written before the name was adopted still resolves.

scene.description: The story beat from knowledge/SCENES-S1-S3.md, not a demo segment letter.

place.description: The map id the scene is set on, sent as the scene block's place (spec 19 section 3).

version.description: Bumped on any edit to the voice or a guard, because the bridge hashes the block into its cache key.

knows.description: The lore limit, in the positive: the only world the persona may speak from.

cannot_say.description: The lore limit, in the negative, written as a category and sent to the model as prose. A category never names the token it forbids.

banned_marks.description: Marks this persona never uses. Konrad never raises his voice, which is a punctuation rule before it is a tone rule.

mood_allowed.description: The moods this persona can be in. An answer outside the list is mapped to the first one and labelled mood_mapped.

fallback_pool.description: The fourth rung for this persona: lines the game owns, so a persona scene always answers with the network off.

lines.description: The bake lines. Fifteen per persona is the card's number, and tools/bake_personas.py refuses a card with fewer.
